explanation: Gift-giving is a well-regarded gesture of goodwill in Turkey, whether visiting someone's home (flowers, chocolates, or pastries are safe choices) or in business (something representative of your home country, good-quality sweets, etc.). Alcohol is best avoided as a gift unless you're confident your host drinks, since many Turks abstain for religious reasons.
local_tip: Bring flowers, chocolates, or a small item from your home country when invited somewhere, and skip alcohol as a gift unless you already know your host drinks.
regional_note: Avoiding alcohol and pork-related gifts matters more in religious or conservative circles and is less of a concern in secular, urban settings.

also_check.note: Gift-giving is highly ritualized; avoid white or red wrapping (funeral colors) and present with both hands.
Gifts can seem unnecessary or suspicious in formal business; if given, keep them small and practical.
Gifts are appreciated but should align with Islamic values (no alcohol or pigskin); avoid giving directly to the opposite gender.

sources.title: Turkey — Business Etiquette, Manners, and Culture
